curiosities: Commodore promoted it as the first 32-bit CD console in Europe.
It is built on the same AGA chipset as the Amiga 1200.
The SX-1 and SX32 add-ons turned it into an Amiga computer with a keyboard and drive ports.
Its processor is a 68EC020 at 14 MHz, with 2 MB of memory.
Its Akiko chip runs the CD drive and speeds up 3D drawing.
An add-on module let it play Video CD films.
A patent dispute kept it out of the US, and Commodore went bankrupt in 1994.
Games save to 1 KB of memory built in.
